facts.statement: Ferganosuchus is an extinct genus containing only one species of gavialid crocodilian.
facts.quote: Ferganosuchus is an extinct monospecific genus of gavialid crocodilian.

facts.statement: Researchers classify Ferganosuchus as a tomistomine, though some suggest it might be a more basal gavialoid.
facts.quote: The genus is thought to be a tomistomine, although it has been suggested that Ferganosuchus may be a more basal gavialoid.

facts.statement: Ferganosuchus is well known because fossils include fairly complete specimens, unlike the fragmentary remains of most other Asian tomistomines.
facts.quote: The genus is well known from fairly complete specimens, unlike most other Asian tomistomines, whose remains tend to be more fragmentary.

facts.statement: Fossils of Ferganosuchus have been found in Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan dating to the Middle Eocene.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found in the region of Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan that date back the middle Eocene.

facts.statement: The genus Ferganosuchus was described by Efimov in 1982.
Ferganosuchus belongs to the family Gavialidae.
The parent group of Ferganosuchus is the subfamily Tomistominae.
The type species of the genus Ferganosuchus is Ferganosuchus planus.
